stages.title: Indirect taxes and subsidies
stages.sub: How government charges and payments on goods shift the supply curve.

steps.q: The government adds £1 to the price of every packet of cigarettes sold. Who actually hands that £1 over to the government, the smoker or the shop?
steps.wrong: The smoker hands it over directly
steps.hint: The smoker pays the shop, then the shop deals with the government.

steps.q: With £1 extra to pay to the government on every packet, is a shop willing to supply the same amount at each price as before?
steps.right: No, it will supply less at each price
steps.wrong: Yes, supply stays exactly the same
steps.hint: The tax adds to the shop's cost of selling each packet, so what happens to the whole supply curve?
